divergences.old: ado work schema --example-only printing the bare example with no envelope
divergences.toil: The flag stays; the example comes back as data in the usual envelope, so with the flag data is the example itself, not { schema, example }. Save .data to use it as an --input-file
divergences.why: Every command writes exactly one envelope, so an agent never has to guess which shape stdout holds. The allowed fields are excused only for calls with --example-only (`when`), so plain ado work schema must still return both.

divergences.old: ado work download-attachment fetching the attachment's relation URL, with the PAT, from whatever host the work item names (#69 item 1)
divergences.toil: The PAT goes only to baseUrl's origin: a relation URL on another host has its path and query re-pointed at baseUrl, with an ADO_ATTACHMENT_HOST warning
divergences.why: A server-supplied URL must not carry the user's credential to a host they didn't configure. A change a principle requires, so a port makes it before a live run (CLAUDE.md, Porting).

divergences.old: ado work download-attachment writing under --dir (default the old CLI's dot-folder in the working directory) anywhere on disk, replacing a file already there, and reporting saved with the platform's separator
divergences.toil: --dir defaults to .toil; the file is written inside the workspace, an existing file is refused with INVALID_INPUT naming the path, and saved uses forward slashes on every platform
divergences.why: A read-only command, whose file name comes from whoever uploaded the attachment, must not change files already on disk or write outside the workspace; paths in JSON output are the same on every platform.

divergences.old: ado project list, pipeline list, pipeline list-runs (with no --top), repo list-builds and repo list-prs paging for as long as the server kept answering
divergences.toil: The same stops (no continuation header, or a short $top/$skip page), plus a bound: after 1,000 pages the command fails with HTTP, naming the list, and a fix to narrow the request
divergences.why: A server that hands back a token or ignores $skip would otherwise be asked forever; the bound turns a hang into an error that says what happened.

divergences.old: ado project list, pipeline list, list-runs, repo list-prs, list-builds and pipeline logs --log-id surfacing a network failure or timeout as Node's bare fetch error, and reading only message from an error body (#69 item 4)
divergences.toil: The same requests, still with no 429 retry; a failure is core's NETWORK, TIMEOUT, AUTH, NOT_FOUND or HTTP error with the server's message and a fix, as every other ado command's is
divergences.why: Errors say plainly what went wrong and what to do next; a bare "fetch failed" says neither.

divergences.old: ado repo delete-comment available to every caller
divergences.toil: The same command on the CLI; toil mcp never serves it
divergences.why: Deletes are never exposed through MCP (CLAUDE.md, Writes).

divergences.old: ado work fields --save and work types --save writing the discovery (discoveredFields, fieldAliases, discoveredTypes) into the global config file
divergences.toil: The flags stay and the result is unchanged, but nothing is written: an ADO_SAVE_UNAVAILABLE warning says so and how to set fieldAliases on the connection. Saved fieldAliases are still read
divergences.why: Area commands never read or write config, so a command an agent can call can't rewrite the user's connections; the core change that would let one save a setting doesn't exist yet.

divergences.old: ado work create and work update printing input-file keys overridden by flags to stderr and in meta.overrides, and work create --parent printing a failed link to stderr
divergences.toil: The same text as ADO_INPUT_OVERRIDDEN and ADO_PARENT_LINK_FAILED entries in meta.warnings; data and the exit code are unchanged
divergences.why: An MCP client never sees stderr, so a warning it can't see would fail silently. meta.warnings is the envelope's place for it (Output Contract).

divergences.old: ado pipeline run --wait giving up with "Timed out waiting for completion after <n>s" as a generic failure
divergences.toil: The same message as a TIMEOUT error, with a fix naming the build id to check
divergences.why: A wait that gives up is a timeout, and the fix says the build may still finish.

divergences.old: A missing collection or project telling the user to run the old CLI's config init
divergences.toil: "Could not determine Azure DevOps collection. Pass --collection, or set collection on the connection." (and the same for project), with a fix naming defaults.ado and the env var
divergences.why: toil has no config init yet; the error names what does exist.

divergences.old: ado work add-attachment typed its data as an attachment with a name
divergences.toil: data is the server's answer passed through unchanged, as before. The upload endpoint answers with an AttachmentReference, { id, url }, so the contract's typed field never existed at run time
divergences.why: Nothing changes; the recorded field came from the old code's type, not from what the server returns, and a fixture shaped like the documented API can't carry it.

divergences.old: ado work fields --type typed each field with a type
divergences.toil: Unchanged: the type-scoped endpoint returns no type or readOnly, so both come out undefined and leave the JSON, as before (#69 item 18, pinned)
divergences.why: A suspected bug is kept until a live run confirms it (CLAUDE.md, Porting); the field is excused only for calls with --type.
